description: GEO metadata JSON template aligned to GEO_template.xlsx (Metadata sheet).
notes: Populate values per GEO_template.xlsx. Keep required fields (prefixed with *) and recommended sample attributes (prefixed with **) as appropriate; leave null/empty if unavailable.

checksums.notes: Provide MD5 checksums for each uploaded raw/processed file to help GEO verify file integrity.

template_source.geo_last_updated_note: This file was last updated by GEO on Dec 17, 2024.

study.description: STUDY section describes the overall GEO Series (GSE) record. Content is displayed publicly and should summarize the experiment at a study level.

*title.description: Overall study title for the GEO Series (GSE). Should be short but descriptive and unique. Avoid overly generic titles.

*summary (abstract).description: Study-level abstract/summary for the GEO Series. Provide background, experimental context, what was measured, and the main goals. 1–3 paragraphs is typical.

*experimental design.description: Describe the experimental design and variables: groups/conditions, timepoints, replicates, controls, randomization, and how samples relate to conditions. Mention any key covariates.

contributor.description: People who contributed to generating the dataset (often authors). Use full names. Include multiple rows if needed.

supplementary file.description: Optional additional files to accompany the GEO Series record (e.g., README, sample metadata CSV, QC reports). Provide file names as they will appear in the submission.

samples.description: SAMPLES section defines one GEO Sample (GSM) per row (one library per row). Titles, library names, and raw files must be unique. Use extra raw/processed columns for technical replicates or multiple outputs.

*library name.description: Unique identifier for each library/sample in this submission. Often corresponds to internal sample ID or library prep ID. Must be unique across rows.

*title.description: Short title for the GEO Sample (GSM). Should uniquely identify the biological material and condition (e.g., 'WT lung, day 7, replicate 1').

*library strategy.description: Sequencing strategy (e.g., RNA-Seq, ChIP-Seq, ATAC-Seq, WGS, scRNA-Seq, etc.). Use controlled terms from GEO/SRA when possible.

*organism.description: Scientific name of the organism (e.g., Homo sapiens, Mus musculus). Should match NCBI Taxonomy naming.

**tissue.description: Tissue of origin (conditional). Use standardized anatomical terms when possible (e.g., UBERON). For single-cell, may be broader organ/tissue source.

**cell line.description: Cell line name if applicable (conditional). Include vendor/catalog and/or accession if available (e.g., ATCC). Leave blank for primary tissue without cell line.

**cell type.description: Cell type (conditional). For scRNA/immune studies, use standard terms (e.g., Cell Ontology) when possible.

genotype.description: Genotype of the sample/organism (e.g., WT, knockout, transgenic allele). Include relevant loci and zygosity if known.

treatment.description: Treatments or perturbations applied (drug, infection, stimulation, vaccination), including dose, route, duration, and time since treatment.

batch.description: Batch identifier capturing known technical batches (prep batch, sequencing run, lane, date). Helps downstream users account for batch effects.

*molecule.description: Molecule extracted for library prep (e.g., total RNA, polyA RNA, genomic DNA, chromatin, nuclei).

*single or paired-end.description: Indicate whether reads are single-end or paired-end. Must be consistent with raw files provided.

*instrument model.description: Sequencing instrument model (e.g., Illumina NovaSeq 6000, NextSeq 2000). Prefer exact model names.

description.description: Additional sample/library description. Useful for specifying finer details not captured elsewhere (e.g., isolation method, enrichment, fraction, indexing scheme).

processed data file.description: Name of processed data file(s) associated with this sample/library (e.g., count matrix, peak calls, BAM, bedGraph). If multiple, list each in separate 'processed data file' columns.

*raw file.description: Name(s) of raw sequencing files for this library (e.g., FASTQ files). For technical replicates, use additional 'raw file' columns. All listed here should also appear in the experiment tables when relevant.

raw file.description: Name(s) of raw sequencing files for this library (e.g., FASTQ files). For technical replicates, use additional 'raw file' columns. All listed here should also appear in the experiment tables when relevant.

protocols.description: PROTOCOLS section captures experimental and computational methods used to generate raw and processed data.

growth protocol.description: Describe how organisms/cells were grown or maintained prior to treatment and collection (media, temperature, passage, housing).

treatment protocol.description: Describe any treatment/perturbation protocol (drug, infection, stimulation, vaccination), including dose, route, timepoints, and controls.

*extract protocol.description: Protocol for extracting the biomolecule (RNA/DNA/chromatin/nuclei). Include kit names, key steps, and any deviations from standard methods.

*library construction protocol.description: Library prep protocol: kit, input amount, fragmentation, barcoding/indexing, amplification cycles, size selection, and any single-cell platform details (e.g., 10x).

*data processing step.description: Describe computational processing steps used to generate processed files (software, versions, parameters, reference genomes, QC thresholds). If multiple steps, list them in order.
validation_hints: Include key parameters (e.g., aligner settings, filtering thresholds)
Describe order of steps if multiple

data processing step.description: Describe computational processing steps used to generate processed files (software, versions, parameters, reference genomes, QC thresholds). If multiple steps, list them in order.

*genome build/assembly.description: Reference genome build/assembly used for alignment/quantification (e.g., GRCh38, mm10). Include release/version if applicable.

*processed data files format and content.field: processed data files format and content
*processed data files format and content.description: Describe each processed data file type, format (e.g., TSV, H5AD, BAM), and what columns/fields contain. Include units and coordinate systems where relevant.

processed data files format and content.field: processed data files format and content
processed data files format and content.template_key: processed data files format and content
processed data files format and content.description: Describe each processed data file type, format (e.g., TSV, H5AD, BAM), and what columns/fields contain. Include units and coordinate systems where relevant.

paired_end_experiments.description: PAIRED-END EXPERIMENTS lists the FASTQ (or equivalent) files for paired-end sequencing. Raw files listed here should also be listed in each sample row under raw file columns.

file name 1.description: Raw read file for mate 1 (R1). FASTQ (or equivalent). Provide the exact file name uploaded.

file name 2.description: Raw read file for mate 2 (R2). FASTQ (or equivalent). Provide the exact file name uploaded.

file name 3.description: Optional additional raw file for the same experiment (e.g., index reads I1/I2, or additional lanes), depending on platform/template guidance.

file name 4.description: Optional additional raw file for the same experiment (e.g., second index read or additional lane).

checksums.description: MD5 checksums for raw and processed files. GEO recommends providing MD5 to verify file integrity after transfer.
